model_annotations.English: Figure 5 presents a grouped bar chart comparing the perplexity of two pruning methods—“Per-Output” (blue bars) and “Per-Layer” (orange bars)—across eight different sparsity rates: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The horizontal axis (x-axis) represents the sparsity rate as categorical labels, while the vertical axis (y-axis) displays perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³, with major tick marks at 10¹, 10², and 10³. At lower sparsity rates (10% to 50%), both methods exhibit similarly low perplexity values, with bars barely rising above the 10¹ mark. As sparsity increases to 60% and beyond, perplexity rises sharply for both methods, with the “Per-Layer” method consistently showing higher perplexity than “Per-Output” at each sparsity level. At 80% sparsity, the “Per-Layer” bar reaches approximately 886.10 (as confirmed by Table 13), while the “Per-Output” bar reaches about 534.42, both approaching the 10³ mark. The chart uses a logarithmic scale to accommodate the large dynamic range of values, as noted in the caption, which also states that the comparison is based on logarithmic results due to the significant difference between high and low sparsity rates. The legend is embedded within the chart, with blue indicating “Per-Output” and orange indicating “Per-Layer”.
